reference.label: Fibre cut
reference.definition: A physical discontinuity in a fibre span that prevents optical signals from passing.
reference.example: Construction work severs a span and receivers beyond the cut detect no light.

reference.label: Increased span loss
reference.definition: Additional attenuation on a fibre span that reduces downstream optical power without fully opening the path.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 8 dB of loss and causes low receive power.

reference.label: Optical connection disconnected
reference.definition: A connector or optical jumper is unplugged, opening the light path at a patching point.
reference.example: A technician removes the pre-amplifier input jumper and composite light disappears.

reference.label: Contaminated connector
reference.definition: Contamination on an optical connector introduces attenuation or reflection into its signal path.
reference.example: Dust on an LC connector raises pre-FEC errors until the connector is cleaned.

reference.label: Amplifier output failure
reference.definition: An optical amplifier or its pump fails completely, producing no optical output.
reference.example: An in-line EDFA loses its pump and drops every wavelength on the span.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: An amplifier delivers less gain than its configured target, reducing downstream power and quality.
reference.example: An EDFA targeted at 18 dB provides only 12 dB of gain.

reference.label: Amplifier noise-figure degradation
reference.definition: An amplifier adds more noise than expected, lowering downstream OSNR despite potentially normal output power.
reference.example: An ageing pre-amplifier maintains output power but lowers all downstream channels' OSNR.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: Amplifier gain becomes uneven across wavelength, leaving some spectral regions lower than others.
reference.example: Long-wavelength edge channels leave an EDFA 3 dB below central channels.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive pump wear causes amplifier pump current to rise in order to maintain gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 121% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: A coherent transmitter's laser fails to emit a usable optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder laser fails and the far-end receiver reports loss of signal.

reference.label: Equipment card failure
reference.definition: A whole equipment card becomes nonfunctional, losing its traffic and valid monitoring.
reference.example: A line card loses power and stops carrying or reporting traffic.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local impairment adds errors or margin penalty without degrading the shared optical path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver develops internal noise while adjacent receivers remain healthy.

reference.label: Transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmit-laser wear is evidenced by increasing bias current before functional failure.
reference.example: Laser bias rises from 100% to 123% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: An optical channel's operating margin declines gradually over time.
reference.example: A channel's estimated margin falls from 4 dB to 1.5 dB over several months.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: The attenuation applied by a WSS to one channel drifts from its configured value.
reference.example: A channel's WSS attenuation increases by 3 dB and its downstream power falls.

reference.label: WSS passband offset
reference.definition: A WSS filter passband shifts away from a channel's nominal centre frequency and penalizes its signal.
reference.example: A WSS filter drifts 8 GHz off centre while measured channel power remains normal.

reference.label: WSS passband narrowing
reference.definition: A WSS presents insufficient usable filter bandwidth and clips part of a channel's spectrum.
reference.example: A narrowed 50 GHz passband clips a 400G signal and raises pre-FEC BER.

reference.label: WSS ingress-port failure
reference.definition: One WSS ingress port fails or blocks all wavelengths arriving on its ROADM degree.
reference.example: The north-degree WSS input fails while channels on other degrees continue normally.

reference.label: Increased differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay rises enough to impose polarization-mode-dispersion penalty on a channel.
reference.example: A fibre route develops 35 ps of DGD and the receiver begins recording errors.

reference.label: Fast polarization transient
reference.definition: The optical state of polarization changes faster than the coherent receiver can track.
reference.example: A lightning-induced disturbance rotates SOP abruptly and briefly disrupts OTU framing.

reference.label: Mechanical loss transient
reference.definition: A brief mechanical disturbance of fibre or patching causes a temporary optical-loss excursion.
reference.example: Movement at a patch panel produces a one-second receive-power dip.

reference.label: Channel-loading transient
reference.definition: Adding or removing WDM channels causes a brief composite-power excursion on an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: Adding several wavelengths produces a short amplifier output-power swing.

reference.label: Protection-switch hit
reference.definition: Protection switching briefly interrupts a protected client service rather than causing a sustained outage.
reference.example: An SNCP changeover interrupts client traffic for 30 ms.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric interrupts the ODUs traversing the switch.
reference.example: A switching-matrix failure interrupts every cross-connected ODU and propagates AIS.

reference.label: ODU cross-connect misconnection
reference.definition: An erroneous OTN cross-connect delivers an ODU to an unintended destination.
reference.example: ODU 7 is connected to the wrong client port and produces a trail-trace mismatch.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: A client-facing port or its optic fails and makes the attached client service unavailable.
reference.example: A failed 100GE client optic takes its service down.

reference.label: Instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring instrument reports an incorrect value rather than the actual measured state.
reference.example: A power monitor reports -20 dBm while an external meter shows -8 dBm.

reference.label: Stale telemetry
reference.definition: A telemetry source repeatedly reports an old frozen value as though it were current.
reference.example: Received-power telemetry remains fixed for an hour despite changing input power.

reference.label: Unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure before the observation point on the signal path.
reference.example: A remote defect is attributed to an upstream failure when its precise source is unknown.

reference.label: Unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure in a lower layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: An ODU fails because of an unidentified defect in its supporting OTU or optical path.

reference.label: Optical signal loss
reference.definition: Optical power is absent or below the receiver's detection threshold.
reference.example: After a fibre is unplugged, the receive photodiode reads below its detection floor.

reference.label: Digital loss of signal
reference.definition: A receiver cannot detect a valid digital symbol stream, whether or not its physical interface remains enabled.
reference.example: A line card asserts dLOS when incoming symbols disappear.

reference.label: Low optical power
reference.definition: Measured optical power is below its expected or configured level.
reference.example: A channel exits a ROADM 3 dB below its target power.

reference.label: Optical power excursion
reference.definition: Optical power undergoes a brief dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Channel loading causes a momentary 2 dB output-power dip.

reference.label: Low OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio is lower than the required or expected level.
reference.example: A noisy amplifier lowers every downstream channel's OSNR by 2 dB.

reference.label: High DGD
reference.definition: Observed differential group delay is elevated enough to threaten signal recovery.
reference.example: A receiver reports 35 ps DGD and increasing frame errors.

reference.label: Filter penalty
reference.definition: Spectral narrowing or misalignment degrades signal quality while optical power may remain normal.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband raises pre-FEC BER although channel power is unchanged.

reference.label: Receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: Signal degradation exists inside one receiver and does not propagate along the optical path.
reference.example: Only one receiver records errors for an otherwise healthy wavelength.

reference.label: Unit down
reference.definition: An equipment unit carries no traffic and provides no valid operational monitoring.
reference.example: A failed line card stops forwarding traffic and its counters become unavailable.

reference.label: Traffic alarms masked
reference.definition: A dominant equipment fault suppresses subordinate signal or traffic alarms.
reference.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL remains visible while the card's LOS and frame alarms are suppressed.
synonyms: traffic alarms masked by equipment alarm

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: An OTN line receiver cannot acquire or maintain OTU frame alignment.
reference.example: Severe noise prevents frame alignment even though optical light remains present.

reference.label: OTU signal degradation
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors exceed the configured degradation threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
reference.example: The receiver crosses its degrade threshold at 0.7 dB estimated margin.

reference.label: Errored second
reference.definition: A one-second interval contains at least one monitored transmission error.
reference.example: Intermittent noise produces 12 errored seconds in a 15-minute interval.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An ODU carries the alarm-indication signal downstream to indicate an upstream defect.
reference.example: After OTU frame loss, each contained ODU carries AIS downstream.

reference.label: OTU backward defect indication
reference.definition: An OTU sink sends backward defect indication toward the remote transmitter after detecting a defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns OTU-BDI to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Misdirected ODU
reference.definition: An ODU is delivered on an incorrect cross-connect path or to the wrong endpoint.
reference.example: The ODU for client A arrives at client B's port.

reference.label: Client service outage
reference.definition: A client service is unable to carry usable traffic in the affected direction.
reference.example: A failed client port stops the customer's 100GE traffic.

reference.label: All optical channels lost
reference.definition: Every wavelength traversing a common optical element or section is simultaneously absent.
reference.example: Failure of an in-line amplifier removes all 80 wavelengths from the following span.

reference.label: OSC loss
reference.definition: The optical supervisory channel is not received on a span.
reference.example: A span cut prevents the next amplifier site from receiving the OSC.

reference.label: No amplifier output
reference.definition: An amplifier has detectable input light but produces no composite optical output.
reference.example: An EDFA receives -12 dBm input but reports zero output power.

reference.label: Amplifier gain out of range
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differs materially from its configured target.
reference.example: An EDFA targeted at 18 dB delivers 15.5 dB.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from target

reference.label: Normal operating state
reference.definition: The referenced path, channel, or equipment continues to meet expected operation.
reference.example: Neighbouring wavelengths remain normal during a single-receiver fault.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver, either currently or in performance-history bins.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports -9.4 dBm received power.

reference.label: Composite amplifier input power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all WDM channels entering an amplifier.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier reports -8 dBm composite input power.

reference.label: Composite amplifier output power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all WDM channels leaving an amplifier.
reference.example: A booster reports +20 dBm composite output power.

reference.label: Pump drive current percentage
reference.definition: Amplifier pump-laser drive current expressed relative to its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier reports pump current at 121% of beginning of life.

reference.label: Transmit laser bias percentage
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current expressed relative to its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transponder reports laser bias at 117% of beginning of life.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for one wavelength, typically by an optical channel monitor.
reference.example: A ROADM OCM reports channel 44 at -3.1 dBm.

reference.label: Optical signal-to-noise ratio
reference.definition: The ratio of optical signal power to optical noise power for a channel, measured or receiver-estimated.
reference.example: A channel monitor reports OSNR of 18.7 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: The bit-error ratio measured by a coherent receiver before forward-error correction.
reference.example: A muxponder reports pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-4.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: The measured delay difference between polarization modes of a received optical signal.
reference.example: A coherent receiver estimates DGD at 22 ps.

reference.label: SOP rate of change
reference.definition: The measured rate at which the received state of polarization changes.
reference.example: The receiver records an SOP rate above its tracking threshold.

reference.label: Line errored-seconds counter
reference.definition: A line-performance counter of errored seconds, commonly retained in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: The line interface records six errored seconds in the current 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Client errored-seconds counter
reference.definition: A client-interface counter of seconds containing monitored client errors.
reference.example: A client port records 14 errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Client unavailable-seconds counter
reference.definition: A client-interface counter of seconds during which the client service is unavailable.
reference.example: A failed client port accumulates 300 unavailable seconds.

reference.label: OSC receiver status
reference.definition: An alarm-oriented indication of whether the optical supervisory channel is being received.
reference.example: An amplifier site reports OSC status as not received after a span cut.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An erbium-doped fibre amplifier used to amplify a multiplexed optical line signal.
reference.example: An EDFA card reports composite input power, output power, gain, and pump current.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A booster raises ROADM output power before the first fibre span.

reference.label: In-line amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at an intermediate line site between terminal nodes.
reference.example: An OLA at an amplifier hut restores power before the next span.

reference.label: Pre-amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier boosts incoming WDM light before the terminal ROADM.

reference.label: Coherent line interface
reference.definition: An interface that transmits or terminates a coherent optical channel.
reference.example: A coherent line interface reports receive power, BER, DGD, and laser health.

reference.label: Coherent transponder
reference.definition: A coherent line interface that maps a client signal onto a line-side optical channel.
reference.example: A VA-TPD-400 terminates one 400G coherent wavelength.

reference.label: Coherent muxponder
reference.definition: A coherent line interface that aggregates multiple client signals onto a line channel.
reference.example: A VA-MXP-400 maps client traffic into a 400G wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A coherent line card that terminates an OTU and its associated optical channel.
reference.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 raises OTU loss of frame when alignment is lost.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: An optical node that independently adds, drops, and routes wavelength channels among degrees.
reference.example: A ROADM routes one west-ingress wavelength south and another east.

reference.label: WSS degree module
reference.definition: The wavelength-selective-switch module serving one directional degree of a ROADM.
reference.example: The north-degree WSS filters and routes wavelengths arriving from the north span.

reference.label: OTN cross-connect switch
reference.definition: An OTN device whose switching fabric cross-connects ODUs between ports.
reference.example: An OTN switch cross-connects an ODU from a line card to a client port.

reference.label: Client interface port
reference.definition: A client-facing interface that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GE client port connects a customer router to an ODU service.

reference.label: OCH loss-of-signal alarm
reference.definition: A channel alarm indicating that a coherent receiver detects no usable optical signal.
reference.example: OCH_LOS is raised after a fibre cut removes light from the receiver.

reference.label: OTU loss-of-frame alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that an OTU receiver cannot maintain frame alignment.
reference.example: OTU_LOF is raised when severe OSNR degradation destroys framing.

reference.label: OTU signal-degrade alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that OTU error performance exceeds its degradation threshold while framing persists.
reference.example: OTU_SD is raised when pre-FEC errors exceed the configured limit.

reference.label: OTU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An alarm showing that the far-end OTU sink has returned a defect indication.
reference.example: The local card raises OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses framing.

reference.label: Transmit-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm reporting an internally detected transmit-laser failure.
reference.example: A failed line laser causes EQPT_TX_FAIL on its card.

reference.label: Card-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm reporting failure of an entire hardware card.
reference.example: A card power-rail fault raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: High laser-bias alarm
reference.definition: A predictive alarm raised when transmit-laser bias exceeds its configured ageing threshold.
reference.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH is raised at 124% of beginning-of-life bias.

reference.label: Amplifier input-loss alarm
reference.definition: An amplifier alarm indicating that no incoming optical light is detected at its input monitor.
reference.example: An OLA raises AMP_INPUT_LOS after the preceding amplifier dies.

reference.label: OMS input-loss alarm
reference.definition: A pre-amplifier alarm indicating loss of composite OMS light at its input.
reference.example: OMS_LOS_P is raised when the OMS input jumper is removed.

reference.label: OSC loss alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that an amplifier site is not receiving the incoming supervisory channel.
reference.example: An OLA raises OSC_LOS after a cut on its incoming span.

reference.label: Amplifier failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that an amplifier has input light but produces no optical output.
reference.example: A booster with normal input and a failed pump raises AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: Amplifier gain-out-of-range alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when measured amplifier gain differs excessively from its target.
reference.example: AMP_GAIN_OOR is raised when an 18 dB target yields only 15.5 dB.

reference.label: Pump end-of-life alarm
reference.definition: An amplifier alarm raised when pump drive current exceeds its end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: AMP_PUMP_EOL is raised when pump current reaches 123% of beginning of life.

reference.label: Client signal-fail alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that a client port cannot provide a valid client service.
reference.example: A client port raises CLIENT_SF when its received ODU is replaced by AIS.

reference.label: ODU-AIS receive alarm
reference.definition: An endpoint alarm indicating receipt of ODU alarm-indication signal, distinct from the AIS signal itself.
reference.example: A destination client port raises ODU_AIS after an upstream OTU defect.

reference.label: ODU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An ODU-layer alarm indicating that the remote ODU endpoint has returned a defect indication.
reference.example: A client port raises ODU_BDI after the far-end ODU sink detects a defect.

reference.label: ODU trace-mismatch alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace differs from the expected identity.
reference.example: ODU_TIM is raised when a port receives another service's trail trace.

reference.label: Protection-active indication
reference.definition: An indication that a protected service is currently selected from its protection path.
reference.example: PROT_ACTIVE is raised after the selector switches away from the working ODU.

reference.label: Protection-unavailable alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that no usable protection path is available for the service.
reference.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when both SNCP paths are defective.

reference.label: Client-port equipment alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating hardware failure of a client port or its optic.
reference.example: A failed 400GE pluggable causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN fabric failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: An OTN switch raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL when its matrix stops forwarding ODUs.

reference.label: Single optical channel
reference.definition: Exactly one wavelength channel rather than the whole multiplexed signal.
reference.example: A drifting WSS setting lowers only channel 37.

reference.label: All multiplexed channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength carried through the referenced common optical element or section.
reference.example: An amplifier outage affects all 80 channels.

reference.label: Subset of channels
reference.definition: More than one but not all channels in a multiplexed optical signal.
reference.example: Gain tilt lowers several long-wavelength edge channels.

reference.label: One receiver only
reference.definition: The particular receiver observing an impairment, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: Internal receiver noise affects receiver A but not receiver B.

reference.label: Every traversing ODU
reference.definition: Every ODU cross-connected through the referenced OTN switch.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupts every ODU traversing the switch.

reference.label: Single ODU
reference.definition: One ODU connection rather than all ODUs or its supporting optical channel.
reference.example: A bad cross-connect misroutes one ODU while other ODUs remain correct.

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing service carried by the referenced client port and ODU connection.
reference.example: A client-port failure takes the attached 100GE service down.

reference.label: Equipment unit
reference.definition: The referenced equipment unit itself rather than the traffic it carries.
reference.example: Pump-current ageing is scoped to one amplifier card.

reference.label: Client-interface port scope
reference.definition: The complete client-facing physical or logical interface affected by a condition.
reference.example: The failure is confined to client port 3 and its attached service.

reference.label: ROADM ingress-port scope
reference.definition: All channels arriving through one ROADM degree's WSS ingress port.
reference.example: Failure of the west ingress blocks every wavelength arriving from the west.

reference.label: Local observing unit
reference.definition: The equipment unit that raises the alarm or observes the condition.
reference.example: Rising pump current and its end-of-life alarm appear on the same amplifier.

reference.label: Local observing port
reference.definition: The particular interface port that raises or observes the condition.
reference.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL identifies the fault on this client port.

reference.label: Immediate upstream span
reference.definition: The fibre span immediately preceding the observing unit in signal-flow direction.
reference.example: A cut on the incoming span removes light at the OLA input.

reference.label: Immediate upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The amplifier immediately preceding the observing unit along the optical path.
reference.example: Input loss at one OLA is traced to the previous EDFA having no output.

reference.label: OMS input
reference.definition: The patching boundary where composite optical light enters an OMS endpoint.
reference.example: A disconnected jumper at the OMS input causes composite-light loss.

reference.label: Upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The channel or its ingress WSS port at the immediately preceding ROADM.
reference.example: Low power is first observed on the channel at the upstream ROADM.

reference.label: Anywhere upstream on the path
reference.definition: Any optical element before the observing unit in the signal's direction of travel.
reference.example: Channel loss may originate at any fibre, amplifier, patch, or ROADM upstream.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting the optical signal toward the observing receiver.
reference.example: OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the optical signal sent by the local transmitter.
reference.example: The far-end receiver reports signal loss after the local laser fails.

reference.label: Path to the far end
reference.definition: The end-to-end signal path between the local unit and its remote line interface.
reference.example: A failed amplifier on the path to the far end removes the transmitted channel.

reference.label: Either client endpoint
reference.definition: Either client-facing endpoint of an end-to-end service.
reference.example: Failure of a client port at either endpoint can take the service down.

reference.label: OTN switch on ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN cross-connect traversed by the referenced ODU service path.
reference.example: A misconnection at an intermediate OTN switch sends the ODU to the wrong port.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route of a protected client service.
reference.example: A defect on the working ODU path triggers selection of protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route reserved to protect a client service.
reference.example: The service switches to the protection ODU after the working path fails.

reference.label: Active ODU path
reference.definition: The working or protection ODU path currently carrying the protected service.
reference.example: A defect on the active ODU path causes the selector to change inputs.

reference.label: Standard monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring supplied by default, including alarms and basic performance counters.
reference.example: A standard line card reports alarms and 15-minute errored-second counters.

reference.label: Power monitoring
reference.definition: An optional capability exposing optical input, output, or receive-power measurements.
reference.example: The power option exposes amplifier composite input and output levels.

reference.label: Optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: Per-wavelength monitoring that supplies channel power and often OSNR at a ROADM.
reference.example: An OCM reports power and OSNR for each WDM wavelength.

reference.label: Advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring that exposes coherent-DSP quality quantities and equipment-health currents.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring reports pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, and laser bias.

reference.label: Fifteen-minute performance bins
reference.definition: Storage and reporting of performance measurements in fixed 15-minute intervals.
reference.example: Client ES and UAS are reported for the interval from 10:00 to 10:15.

reference.label: Hard fault
reference.definition: An abrupt persistent fault that causes immediate traffic or signal loss.
reference.example: A fibre cut producing instant loss of signal is a hard fault.

reference.label: Soft degradation
reference.definition: An impairment that reduces quality while traffic or signal presence may continue.
reference.example: A 2 dB OSNR penalty with frames still aligned is a soft degradation.

reference.label: Incipient fault
reference.definition: A slow warning trend that precedes failure without yet causing an outage.
reference.example: Rising laser-bias current before transmitter failure is incipient.

reference.label: Transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less rather than a persistent fault.
reference.example: A short polarization disturbance causing a momentary error burst is transient.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: The highest alarm priority for severe service or network impact requiring immediate attention.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupting every ODU is assigned critical severity.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: A high alarm priority for significant service impact below critical priority.
reference.example: Loss of one client service is assigned major severity.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: A lower alarm priority for a limited or nonurgent operational issue.
reference.example: An ageing warning while service remains healthy is assigned minor severity.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: The state is reported or monitored as a condition without generating an alarm.
reference.example: A normal operating observation is marked not alarmed.

reference.label: Pass-through behavior
reference.definition: A device forwards an arriving impairment without removing or terminating it.
reference.example: An input OSNR penalty remains present at an amplifier's output.

reference.label: Default condition handling
reference.definition: The fallback handling applied to an arriving condition when no more specific rule matches.
reference.example: An unclassified optical impairment follows the unit's default pass-through rule.

reference.label: OTU consequent-action behavior
reference.definition: Loss of OTU frame causes downstream ODU-AIS insertion and backward OTU-BDI transmission.
reference.example: An OTU receiver losing frame sends AIS on contained ODUs and BDI toward the transmitter.

reference.label: Span-local OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and originates a new OSC on the next span.
reference.example: Hut B terminates Hut A's OSC and launches a fresh OSC toward Hut C.

reference.label: SNCP protection behavior
reference.definition: A receive-side selector chooses between working and protection ODU paths for a client service.
reference.example: When the working ODU develops AIS, the client port selects the healthy protection ODU.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM switching
reference.definition: A ROADM switches wavelengths independently, so ingress-wide impairments continue on each routed channel.
reference.example: West-ingress channels retain their common OSNR penalty after being routed to different egress degrees.

reference.label: Automatic amplifier gain control
reference.definition: An amplifier adjusts pump drive to maintain configured gain as input power changes.
reference.example: With gain held at 18 dB, a 3 dB input drop produces a 3 dB output drop.

reference.label: Span-loss gain provisioning
reference.definition: An amplifier's turn-up gain target is set to compensate the attenuation of the associated fibre span.
reference.example: A booster is provisioned for 17 dB gain to match a measured 17 dB span loss.
synonyms: gain target provisioned to span loss

reference.label: ROADM power leveling
reference.definition: A ROADM adjusts attenuation to restore a channel within its available leveling range.
reference.example: The ROADM reduces attenuation by 2 dB and restores the channel's output power.

reference.label: Persistent OSNR penalty after leveling
reference.definition: Restoring channel power at a node does not remove noise already added upstream.
reference.example: A ROADM restores power to target while the channel retains its 2 dB OSNR penalty.
